message.content:
Here’s a quick snapshot of some of the most famous American composers across different eras and genres:

| Era / Genre | Composer | Notable Works |
|-------------|----------|---------------|
| **Early American Classical** | **William Billings** (1746–1800) | *“New England Psalm”* |
| | **John Philip Sousa** (1854–1932) | “The Stars and Stripes Forever” |
| | **George Gershwin** (1898–1937) | “Rhapsody in Blue,” “An American in Paris” |
| **20th‑Century Classical & Film** | **Aaron Copland** (1900–1990) | “Appalachian Spring,” “Fanfare for the Common Man” |
| | **Leonard Bernstein** (1918–1990) | “West Side Story,” “Candide” |
| | **Philip Glass** (born 1937) | *Glassworks*, *Einstein on the Beach* |
| | **John Williams** (born 1942) | Scores for *Star Wars*, *Indiana Jones*, *Jurassic Park* |
| | **Danny Elfman** (born 1953) | Scores for *Batman*, *The Nightmare Before Christmas* |
| | **Hans Zimmer** (born 1957) | Scores for *Inception*, *The Dark Knight*, *Interstellar* |
| **Contemporary Classical & Experimental** | **Steve Reich** (born 1936) | *Music for 18 Musicians*, *Different Trains* |
| | **John Adams** (born 1947) | *Nixon in China*, *Short Ride in a Fast Machine* |
| | **Jennifer Higdon** (born 1962) | *Blue Cathedral*, *Piano Concerto* |
| | **Esa-Pekka Salonen** (born 1958) | *Violin Concerto*, *Graal-Daemon* |
| **Jazz & Popular Music** | **Duke Ellington** (1899–1974) | “Mood Indigo,” “It Don’t Mean a Thing” |
| | **Miles Davis** (1926–1991) | *Kind of Blue*, *Bitches Brew* |
| | **Herbie Hancock** (born 1940) | *Head Hunters*, *Cantaloupe Island* |
| | **Bob Dylan** (born 1941) | *Like a Rolling Stone*, *Blowin’ in the Wind* |
| | **Taylor Swift** (born 1989) | *Folklore*, *Evermore* |

These composers have had a profound impact on American music, shaping everything from classical orchestral repertoire to film scores, jazz, and popular music. Their works continue to be performed worldwide and studied by musicians and scholars alike.
